title: Verify Rohan's personal emergency bag
openingNarrative: Rohan is still in ICU. Discharge and community planning cannot wait until the bay door. The team must verify his personal emergency bag—the community transfer kit used at home, school, and DisabilityFour events—before continuity plans harden. Paid trained responders own the inventory; family and Jay are not unpaid clinicians stocking the bag. Redundancy is not excess: one worker handles the airway; another handles the rest of the emergency. Rohan is addressed first. The checklist and a curated strip of critical stills are on the table—not all fifty-six items at once.
clinicalState: Still ICU. Physiology carries forward from sedation and airway branches. Community bag readiness is a planning domain mid-ICU: airway spares, suction and power, AAC access kit, and governance documents. No medication doses or prescribing. Sensitive medication compartments stay labelled only.

choices.label: Prioritise airway and power redundancy — trach spares, suction, circuits, batteries, chargers
choices.immediateConsequence: Home readiness rises and airway obstruction risk falls because spare tubes, portable suction, circuits, and charged power are confirmed for transfer. Other kit domains may feel unfinished; family burden ticks up if fear of incompleteness elsewhere grows.
choices.delayedConsequence: Communication-access and governance packs still need a dated review before school return. Redundancy without docs or AAC is incomplete community readiness.
choices.rohanAacLine: EVERY ALARM STILL DESERVES AN ANSWER.

choices.label: Prioritise communication-access kit — AAC offline, cheek switch, boards, vocabulary, large print
choices.immediateConsequence: Communication access, authorship control, and school access rise because offline AAC, spare cheek switch, and low-tech boards travel with Rohan. Airway hardware may still need a second pass before discharge.
choices.delayedConsequence: Access at wake and at school events depends on this kit; power and trach redundancy remain separate paid-responder checks.

choices.label: Prioritise governance docs — airway plan, contacts, handover, privacy/dignity, revision date
choices.immediateConsequence: Privacy protection and public trust rise; home readiness improves modestly because current airway plan, contacts, checklist, and dignity guidelines are verified for handover.
choices.delayedConsequence: Docs without charged batteries or offline AAC still fail a real transfer. Revision date must stay current before school membership plans lock.

disabilityRightsNotes: Rohan's personal emergency bag is for paid trained responders—not unpaid family labour.
Redundancy is not excess: one worker airway, one worker rest-of-emergency.
Communication access equipment is emergency equipment.
Privacy and dignity guidelines travel with the kit; crisis is not public property.
debriefNotes: Kit prioritisation is a trade-off with no single correct answer.
Pairs with home/school continuity: staffing plans need a verified bag.
Sensitive medication cards stay non-prescriptive—labels only.
